title: Gateway Partnership Act

claims.claim: The National Park Service is the party that signs the one-time agreement.
claims.sourceSpan: The Secretary, in accordance with subsection (b), may enter into a one-time agreement
claims.note: Source attaches the agreement authority to 'the Secretary' (defined as the Secretary of the Interior). NPS is the Interior bureau that administers Gateway Arch National Park, so 'National Park Service' is a plain-English gloss on the signing party, not a fabricated account. Non-material; the sections detail correctly names 'The Secretary of the Interior.'

claims.claim: The agreement is a one-time agreement.
claims.sourceSpan: may enter into a one-time agreement

claims.claim: The agreement is with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation.
claims.sourceSpan: means the Gateway Arch Park Foundation, a nonprofit organization that serves as the official philanthropic partner of the Park
claims.note: SEC. 3(a) reads 'with the Foundation'; SEC. 2(1) defines Foundation as the Gateway Arch Park Foundation.

claims.claim: The agreement is to hold private events at Gateway Arch National Park.
claims.sourceSpan: to host private events at the Park, which may include the use of Park buildings
claims.note: Park defined as Gateway Arch National Park in SEC. 2(2).

claims.claim: Private events may be held inside Park buildings like the Arch Visitor Center and the Old Courthouse.
claims.sourceSpan: the Arch Visitor Center; (B) the Old Courthouse; and (C) any other building administered or managed by the Secretary as part of the Park that is open to the public

claims.claim: The agreement can last up to five years.
claims.sourceSpan: for a period not to exceed five years

claims.claim: The agreement must include terms protecting the Park.
claims.sourceSpan: shall include terms and conditions to protect the resources and values of the Park
claims.note: 'shall include' = must. Direction preserved.

claims.claim: The agreement must charge fees that cover the government's costs.
claims.sourceSpan: shall charge a fee to cover the cost of maintaining the Park and Park buildings with respect to wear and tear resulting from the private events
claims.note: The MANDATORY fee (SEC. 3(d)(1)) covers wear-and-tear maintenance cost only; recovery of ALL costs (SEC. 3(d)(2)) is DISCRETIONARY ('may recover'). 'must charge fees that cover the government's costs' slightly broadens the mandatory scope. Non-material; top_lines separates the mandatory fee from discretionary full recovery correctly.

claims.claim: Authorizes a one-time agreement letting the Gateway Arch Park Foundation host private, paid events.
claims.sourceSpan: may enter into a one-time agreement for a period not to exceed five years with the Foundation to host private events at the Park
claims.note: 'paid' sourced to the mandatory fee in SEC. 3(d)(1) ('shall charge a fee').

claims.claim: It is a National Park Service agreement.
claims.sourceSpan: The Secretary, in accordance with subsection (b), may enter into a one-time agreement
claims.note: Same NPS-vs-Secretary gloss as summary; source names 'the Secretary' (of the Interior). Plain-English, non-material.

claims.claim: Events are held in Gateway Arch National Park buildings.
claims.sourceSpan: to host private events in Gateway Arch National Park buildings

claims.claim: The term is no more than five years.
claims.sourceSpan: for a period not to exceed five years

claims.claim: Sponsored by a Democrat with 2 cosponsors.
claims.note: From cache sponsor (D-MO-1) / cosponsors (2) fields; structural per rubric class 8. Not in bill text.

claims.note: Breadth-of-support characterization; not in source. Rubric class 8 flags breadth-of-support claims. Non-material style debt.

claims.note: Not in bill text (EH engrossed version) and not present in cache versions[] (which shows only 'Referred in Senate' 2026-03-17, no committee-reported action). Unverifiable process claim; non-material framing debt.

claims.claim: Its narrow scope is a one-time partnership at a single national park.
claims.sourceSpan: may enter into a one-time agreement for a period not to exceed five years with the Foundation
claims.note: 'one-time' and single-park (Gateway Arch) are bill-content facts.

claims.claim: Private Events at Gateway Arch (Section 3).
claims.sourceSpan: to host private events at the Park, which may include the use of Park buildings

claims.claim: One-time National Park Service agreement with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation.
claims.sourceSpan: may enter into a one-time agreement for a period not to exceed five years with the Foundation
claims.note: 'one-time' and 'with the Foundation' sourced; 'National Park Service' is the same Secretary-of-the-Interior gloss (non-material).

claims.claim: Agreement term capped at five years.
claims.sourceSpan: for a period not to exceed five years

claims.claim: Covers the Arch Visitor Center, Old Courthouse, and other public Park buildings.
claims.sourceSpan: the Arch Visitor Center; (B) the Old Courthouse; and (C) any other building administered or managed by the Secretary as part of the Park that is open to the public
claims.note: 'other public Park buildings' matches (C) 'open to the public'.

claims.claim: Cost Recovery and Safeguards (Section 3).
claims.sourceSpan: may recover all costs incurred as a result of the private events
claims.note: Cost recovery in SEC. 3(d); safeguards in SEC. 3(b) terms and conditions.

claims.claim: Secretary must charge fees for event wear-and-tear.
claims.sourceSpan: shall charge a fee to cover the cost of maintaining the Park and Park buildings with respect to wear and tear resulting from the private events
claims.note: 'must' = 'shall'; mandatory. Correctly attributes to the Secretary.

claims.claim: Government may recover all event costs, including security and personnel.
claims.sourceSpan: may recover all costs incurred as a result of the private events and use of the Park and Park buildings, including maintenance, utilities, administrative expenses, security, and personnel costs
claims.note: 'may recover' = discretionary; direction preserved. Security and personnel listed verbatim.

claims.claim: Foundation must carry liability insurance naming the United States.
claims.sourceSpan: liability insurance in an amount sufficient to protect the interests of the United States that lists the United States as additionally insured
claims.note: Agreement is with the Foundation and lists the US as additionally insured, implying the Foundation is the primary insured; reasonable inference. 'naming the United States' = 'lists the United States as additionally insured.'

claims.claim: Limits and Sunset (Section 3).
claims.sourceSpan: The authority to enter into and carry out an agreement with the Foundation pursuant to this Act shall sunset
claims.note: Sunset in SEC. 3(f); use limits in SEC. 3(c).

claims.claim: Authority sunsets 7 years after enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: shall sunset on the date that is 7 years after the date of enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Events cannot disrupt public access to the Park.
claims.sourceSpan: shall not take place during times or in locations that prevent or disrupt public use or access to the Park or Park buildings

claims.claim: Report to Congress due within 4 years.
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 4 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate a report

claims.claim: Section 3 — Gateway Arch National Park Partner Agreement Pilot Project.
claims.sourceSpan: GATEWAY ARCH NATIONAL PARK PARTNER AGREEMENT PILOT PROJECT

claims.claim: Authorizes a one-time agreement, for a period not to exceed five years, letting the Gateway Arch Park Foundation host private events at the Park, which may include the use of Park buildings.
claims.sourceSpan: may enter into a one-time agreement for a period not to exceed five years with the Foundation to host private events at the Park, which may include the use of Park buildings
claims.note: Near-verbatim restatement.

claims.claim: The Secretary of the Interior may enter the agreement.
claims.sourceSpan: The Secretary, in accordance with subsection (b), may enter into a one-time agreement
claims.note: Correctly names the Secretary of the Interior (SEC. 2(4) definition).

claims.claim: The agreement must include terms protecting the Park's resources.
claims.sourceSpan: shall include terms and conditions to protect the resources and values of the Park

claims.claim: Terms include exclusive-use dates and times.
claims.sourceSpan: dates and times during which the Foundation may be the exclusive organization that holds a special event in specified Park buildings

claims.claim: Terms include a maximum number of events per month.
claims.sourceSpan: the maximum number of events that can be held per month

claims.claim: Terms include National Park Service staffing levels.
claims.sourceSpan: appropriate National Park Service staffing levels necessary to ensure public safety and resource protection during such events

claims.claim: Terms include liability insurance listing the United States as additionally insured.
claims.sourceSpan: liability insurance in an amount sufficient to protect the interests of the United States that lists the United States as additionally insured

claims.claim: Events must be consistent with the Park's purposes.
claims.sourceSpan: consistent with the purposes of the Park

claims.claim: Events may not disrupt public use or access.
claims.sourceSpan: shall not take place during times or in locations that prevent or disrupt public use or access to the Park or Park buildings

claims.claim: Requires the Secretary to charge a fee covering event wear-and-tear.
claims.sourceSpan: shall charge a fee to cover the cost of maintaining the Park and Park buildings with respect to wear and tear resulting from the private events
claims.note: 'shall charge' = requires; mandatory direction preserved.

claims.claim: Allows recovery of all costs incurred from the private events.
claims.sourceSpan: may recover all costs incurred as a result of the private events and use of the Park and Park buildings
claims.note: 'allows' = 'may'; discretionary direction preserved.

claims.claim: Recoverable costs include maintenance, utilities, administrative expenses, security, and personnel.
claims.sourceSpan: including maintenance, utilities, administrative expenses, security, and personnel costs

claims.claim: Nothing in the Act prevents the National Park Service from hosting its own events or issuing permits to other parties.
claims.sourceSpan: Nothing in this Act prevents the National Park Service from hosting events or issuing permits to other individuals or entities for special events or otherwise

claims.claim: Sunsets the agreement authority 7 years after enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: shall sunset on the date that is 7 years after the date of enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Requires a report to Congress within 4 years.
claims.sourceSpan: Not later than 4 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit

claims.claim: Any existing agreement also terminates at the seven-year mark.
claims.sourceSpan: Any existing agreement entered into under this section shall terminate, notwithstanding any terms within such agreement, on the date that is 7 years after the date of enactment of this Act

claims.claim: The report goes to the House Committee on Natural Resources and the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
claims.sourceSpan: the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate

claims.claim: The report must cover operational impacts on visitor access, security, staffing, and facilities.
claims.sourceSpan: operational impacts of the agreement on visitor access, security, staffing, and facilities management

claims.claim: The report must cover financial results including fees collected and costs recovered.
claims.sourceSpan: financial implications of the agreement, including fees collected and costs recovered

claims.claim: The required agreement terms must include a provision stating the Federal Government will not be held liable for injuries or deaths from any cause resulting from the Foundation's occupancy and use of specified Park buildings.
claims.sourceSpan: a provision stating that the Federal Government and agents and employees of the Federal Government will not be held liable for claims for damages or suits for any injuries or deaths from any cause resulting from the occupancy and use of specified Park buildings by the Foundation
claims.note: Binding matches: heading over the span is SEC. 3(b)(4). 'from any cause' verbatim.

claims.claim: This term shifts injury-and-death liability during private events away from the United States regardless of cause.
claims.sourceSpan: will not be held liable for claims for damages or suits for any injuries or deaths from any cause resulting from the occupancy and use of specified Park buildings by the Foundation
claims.note: 'regardless of cause' = 'from any cause'; characterization grounded in the liability-waiver text.

claims.claim: The bill requires the agreement to set a maximum number of events per month but does not set that cap itself.
claims.sourceSpan: the maximum number of events that can be held per month
claims.note: Provable absence: text requires the term but states no numeric cap.

claims.claim: The bill limits the agreement to the Gateway Arch Park Foundation but does not address the agreement if the Foundation stops serving as the Park's philanthropic partner.
claims.sourceSpan: means the Gateway Arch Park Foundation, a nonprofit organization that serves as the official philanthropic partner of the Park
claims.note: Provable absence: no contingency provision for the Foundation ceasing to be the philanthropic partner.

claims.claim: The bill requires the Secretary to recover costs and report on fees collected.
claims.sourceSpan: shall charge a fee to cover the cost of maintaining the Park and Park buildings with respect to wear and tear resulting from the private events
claims.note: The mandatory element is the wear-and-tear FEE (SEC. 3(d)(1), 'shall charge'); recovery of ALL costs is discretionary (SEC. 3(d)(2), 'may recover'). Reporting on fees collected is required (SEC. 3(h)(2)). 'requires the Secretary to recover costs' slightly overstates the mandatory scope but the fee-charging duty and reporting duty are real. Non-material.

claims.claim: The bill does not direct where recovered funds are deposited or how they may be spent.
claims.sourceSpan: may recover all costs incurred as a result of the private events and use of the Park and Park buildings
claims.note: Provable absence: no deposit/expenditure destination stated for recovered funds.

claims.claim: A one-time National Park Service authority to enter a private-events agreement with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation, sunsetting 7 years after enactment.
claims.sourceSpan: may enter into a one-time agreement for a period not to exceed five years with the Foundation
claims.note: One-time authority + Foundation + 7-year sunset all sourced; 'National Park Service' is the recurring Secretary-of-the-Interior gloss (non-material).

claims.claim: Authority for the Secretary to charge fees and recover all costs from the private events.
claims.sourceSpan: shall charge a fee to cover the cost of maintaining the Park and Park buildings with respect to wear and tear resulting from the private events
claims.note: Charge fees (shall, SEC. 3(d)(1)) + recover all costs (may, SEC. 3(d)(2)). Correctly attributes to the Secretary.

claims.claim: The agreement's modification/cancellation clause — modification or cancellation is allowed, but any modified agreement must still comply with terms (1) through (4) — is not surfaced.
claims.sourceSpan: a provision allowing for the modification or cancellation of the terms and conditions of the agreement, except that any modified agreement shall still comply with the terms and conditions described in subparagraphs (1) through (4)
claims.note: Secondary administrative term; the core protective terms (1)-(4) are covered. Non-material.

claims.claim: The use limit barring activities that degrade the integrity, appearance, or purposes of the Park is not surfaced.
claims.sourceSpan: shall not include activities that degrade the integrity, appearance, or purposes of the Park
claims.note: Analysis covers SEC. 3(c)(1)(A) (consistent with purposes) and (c)(3) (no disruption) but not the (c)(2) degradation bar. Non-material.

claims.claim: The requirement that events be compatible with National Park Service programs is not surfaced.
claims.sourceSpan: compatible with National Park Service programs
claims.note: Analysis notes 'consistent with the Park's purposes' (c)(1)(A) but drops the (c)(1)(B) NPS-program-compatibility limb. Non-material.

claims.claim: The saving clause preserving the Secretary's other authority to issue special use permits or agreements is not surfaced.
claims.sourceSpan: Nothing in this Act affects any other authority of the Secretary to issue special use permits or agreements
claims.note: Distinct from the SEC. 3(e) NPS-events saving clause the analysis does cover. Non-material.

notes: Amendment/authorization bill (H.R. 5254 Engrossed in House). No referencedSources registered; audited against bill text only (full read, 5455 chars). All figures (five-year term, 7-year sunset, 4-year report deadline) and directions (mandatory 'shall charge' fee vs. discretionary 'may recover' all costs; 7-year sunset; liability waiver 'from any cause') verified verbatim — no material issues. Recurring non-material item: summary/brief/top_lines[0].subs[0]/changes.added[0] name 'National Park Service' as the agreement party, while the source attaches the authority to 'the Secretary' (of the Interior, SEC. 2(4)); NPS is the administering Interior bureau, so it is a plain-English gloss, and the sections detail names the Secretary correctly. likelihoodReason open rows are framing/process claims not in bill text (suspension-of-the-rules, broad-bipartisan-agreement path, Senate ENR reported-without-amendment, little-organized-opposition, Senate-floor-time forecast) — non-material style debt per rubric class 8. Four minor omissions: SEC. 3(b)(5) modification/cancellation clause, SEC. 3(c)(2) degradation bar, SEC. 3(c)(1)(B) NPS-program compatibility, SEC. 3(g) saving clause.
